2610.08586.title: MINDSET: Energy-based Schema Evolution for Long Conversational Agent Memory
2610.08586.paper_summary: Long conversational agents have become essential in our daily lives. They must remember what was said long back in order to help us efficiently complete a task without needing the user to repeat instructions and context repeatedly. However, the main issue is that instructions and context change over time and so the agents must be able to adapt accordingly. A useful memory system should preserve both current and historical states, distinguish stale information from active knowledge, retrieve evidence appropriate to the query and avoid repeatedly invoking a large language model to rewrite prior interactions. We introduce MINDSET, a memory controller that stores a conversation as immutable episodes and organizes them into versioned schemas through minimum-energy state transitions. Each incoming episode may reinforce, supersede, split or create a schema. The transition decision balances representation distortion, contradiction, historical damage, fragmentation and internal inconsistency, while hysteresis prevents isolated contradictions from prematurely rewriting stable memory. We evaluate MINDSET against 5 memory systems on a reproducible sample of 850 questions (700 LoCoMo + 150 MemoryAgentBench). MINDSET obtains the highest observed LoCoMo answer F1 while significantly improving retrieval ranking (Recall@8, MRR and nDCG@8) over the second best method LightMem (p<0.01 after Holm correction). It obtains the highest observed scores on MemoryAgentBench although the relative difference is low. Ablations identify controlled fragmentation and schema-aware assignment as the largest contributors to answer quality. Additionally, a 700-question cross-model evaluation with GLM-4.7 and Gemma-4-31B supported model independence. These results show that long-term memory can be better handled as constrained state management rather than continual summarization.
2610.08586.paper_summary_zh: 長期對話代理已成為我們日常生活中不可或缺的一部分。它們必須記住很久以前所說的內容，以便有效地幫助我們完成任務，而無需用戶重複指示和背景。然而，主要問題在於指示和背景隨著時間而變化，因此代理必須能夠相應地適應。一個有用的記憶系統應該保留當前和歷史狀態，區分過時的信息和活躍的知識，檢索與查詢相關的證據，並避免重複調用大型語言模型來重寫先前的交互。我們介紹了MINDSET，一個記憶控制器，它將對話存儲為不可變的事件，並通過最小能量狀態轉換將其組織成版本化的架構。每個進入的事件可以強化、取代、拆分或創建一個架構。轉換決策平衡表示失真、矛盾、歷史損害、碎片化和內部不一致，而遲滯則防止孤立的矛盾過早地重寫穩定記憶。我們在850個問題（700個LoCoMo + 150個MemoryAgentBench）的可重複樣本上評估MINDSET，與5個記憶系統進行比較。MINDSET獲得了觀察到的最高LoCoMo答案F1，同時顯著改善了檢索排名（Recall@8、MRR和nDCG@8），超過第二好的方法LightMem（p<0.01經Holm修正後）。它在MemoryAgentBench上獲得了觀察到的最高分數，儘管相對差異較小。消融實驗確定了受控碎片化和架構感知分配是答案質量的最大貢獻者。此外，與GLM-4.7和Gemma-4-31B的700個問題跨模型評估支持模型獨立性。這些結果顯示，長期記憶可以更好地作為受限狀態管理來處理，而不是持續的總結。
